name: model1_split_101_25_84_v1
description: Approved Model 1 case split: first 101 cases train, next 25 validation, last 84 (official test) test. Chronological and incident-group-aware.
ordering: cases.csv file order (strictly ascending timestamp); chronological, no random assignment

sample_time_boundaries.rule: AD split time (lies inside the safe gap)

checks.detail: case timestamps strictly increase in file order; splits are contiguous index ranges in that order
every class appears in every split
split-classes below 3 cases (per-class metrics unstable): {'validation': {'Node Memory': 1}}
175 incident groups, none spans two splits
every boundary has a positive safe gap (>= 1950 s after allowing 719 s of window reach)
every case's history + window lies inside its split's time period
held-out set equals ARMOR's last 84 cases; no official test case moved
AD split 1651852800 (sample-based, 60% of samples) vs first held-out case 1651858208 (case-based, 60% of cases): AD boundary is 5408 s earlier; FT/RCL use cases only, AD uses samples

approval.basis: nearest boundary to the proposed 100 with a positive safe gap and no cut incident group (see boundary_scan.json)

scope.this_manifest: Model 1 case-level split: which injection cases are used for training, validation and testing.
scope.sample_level_ad_timeline: ARMOR's anomaly-detection split is sample-based (60% of the 7,200 samples = the AD split time) and is unchanged; the validation|test sample boundary here is aligned to it, so every post-AD-boundary sample belongs to the test period.
scope.official_armor_protocol: official_armor_v1 (126 / 84 by case order) is preserved unchanged for reproduction; the 84 test cases are identical in both.
scope.detection_evaluation: reported as two separate event-level populations (98 official AD events, 84 documented injection cases); never averaged

statistical_limitations: Validation contains a single Node Memory case: Node Memory validation metrics (recall, F1, macro-F1 contribution) are statistically unstable and must not be used to tune hyper-parameters or thresholds on their own.
Node Memory has only 4 training and 4 test cases; per-class test estimates for it have very wide uncertainty.
Validation Node CPU has 3 cases; treat per-class validation numbers as indicative only.
No incident end times exist: this split assigns cases, it does not define sample-level detection labels.
